text:
Maya (Sales): Heads up — prospect 'Galileo Health' wants a 2-week POC next week using a customer-provided fine-tuned variant (galileo-7b-4bit). Need a quick preflight checklist: variant compatibility, KV cache persistence, private deployment + KMS/HSM, and a rough pricing delta for quant vs fp16. Kickoff target: Tue morning. Any immediate blockers?

Ravi (Eng-ML): Quick clarifying Qs: does the variant use the same tokenizer as the base galileo model? Any custom CUDA ops (custom attention kernels / fused ops)? What's the max sequence length they expect to hit?

Maya (Sales): I'll ask them for the HF repo link and the model card. They mentioned 4k sequence lengths for a subset of calls. No mention of custom ops yet.

Ravi (Eng-ML): Ok — rough notes:
- Tokenizer mismatch is the most common blocker. If they changed tokenization we need to validate decoding.
- Custom ops: if the variant depends on proprietary kernels not in our runtime we'll need a compatibility shim or to build the op (can delay).
- 4k seqs are fine but affects memory; will influence batching strategy.
- 4-bit quant usually supported by our runtime (per-channel/group quantization OK), but need to scan the artifact.
- KV cache persistence: Hosted = ephemeral per-session; Dedicated/Private can enable persisted session KV with config.

ops-bot: Model scan queued (job id 7729). I will post results here when complete.

Devon (Solutions): Customer specifically requires Private/VPC + HSM-backed KMS for keys. They also want a canary/fallback to an open model if the variant misbehaves. Can we support that without extra engineering?

Ravi (Eng-ML): Smart routing supports fallback to a compatible family (we can route to galileo-7b-open or a smaller galileo variant). We do need the model to be onboarded into our catalog with a compatible_fallback tag.
For HSM-backed KMS: Private supports customer-managed KMS; HSM add-on requires SOC/Legal review and takes extra lead time.

Priya (Security): Please get the completed security questionnaire and provenance for the model (training data summary, third-party dependencies). Also need their data retention and PII handling SOPs before approving Private/HSM. Marking as high priority for enterprise review.

Maya (Sales): Good call. If they can't share the repo immediately, what's the minimal path to start a POC (so the timeline doesn't slip)?

Ravi (Eng-ML): Minimal to start:
- Hosted sandbox endpoint with ACLs + pinned uploaded artifact (if license allows hosting customer model).
- Ephemeral KV cache (no persisted sessions).
- Basic monitoring only.
This lets them start tests while we finish Private/HSM and security review. Pricing: very rough ballpark — hosted 4-bit inference ~35–50% cheaper per-token compared to fp16 in our telemetry; estimate: hosted 4-bit ~ $0.008 per 1k-token equivalent request (ballpark for initial quote). We'll produce a proper quote once we know expected QPS/seq-length.

Devon (Solutions): I'll put together a quote matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private + KMS/HSM add-on + onboarding effort). ETA: EOD today.

Maya (Sales): I'll ask them for the HF link, model card, and the security questionnaire now. Will post the link in this thread. Thanks all! :rocket:

Ravi (Eng-ML): Once ops-bot posts the scan results I'll list any required runtime changes (if any). If scan is clean we can fast-track hosted POC.

ops-bot: Model scan complete (job id 7729) — results: tokenization: match, no custom ops detected, quant format: 4-bit group-wise per-channel. Recommended: onboardable to hosted as-is; for persisted KV recommend Dedicated.

Maya (Sales): Amazing — forwarding to customer now. Scheduling kickoff Tue but will confirm once they return the questionnaire.

Devon (Solutions): Noted. Preparing quote drafts.

Priya (Security): I'll draft the initial review checklist so we can parallelize legal/security checks.

Maya (Sales): Thanks everyone — will update here when I have the repo and questionnaire. :thumbsup:
